articles.title: Independent predictors of non-suicidal self-injury among adolescents: a logistic regression model development study based on coping styles
articles.author: Qiuyu Yuan
articles.summary: ObjectiveNon-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is an urgent and substantial public health concern among adolescents. This study is aimed at identifying the independent psychological predictors of NSSI and developing and validating a logistic regression-based risk discrimination model focused on coping styles.MethodsA cross-sectional study involving 206 adolescents (104 with NSSI and 102 healthy controls) was conducted. All the participants provided general demographic data, and completed the Experiences in Close Relationships Inventory (ECR), the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire-Short Form Version (CTQ-SF), and the Coping Styles Questionnaire (CSQ). articles.author: Weihan Yuan
articles.summary: BackgroundPerceived social support is an important psychosocial resource for competitive athletes, while perceived stress is closely associated with athlete burnout. articles.title: The mediating role of smartphone addiction in the relationship between desire for being liked and psychological resilience
articles.author: Ahmet Yavuz Mallı
articles.summary: PurposeThis study examined the association between the desire for being liked and psychological resilience among university students enrolled in faculties of sports sciences in Türkiye and investigated whether smartphone addiction statistically mediated this association.MethodA cross-sectional correlational design was employed. Participants were 237 university students (159 males and 78 females) enrolled in faculties of sports sciences in Türkiye, recruited using a convenience sampling method. Data were collected using the Desire for Being Liked Scale, the Smartphone Addiction Scale–Short Version, and the Brief Resilience Scale. Pearson correlation analysis and a bootstrap mediation analysis (PROCESS Macro Model 4; 5,000 resamples) were conducted to examine the indirect association between the variables. Gender was included as a covariate in the mediation analysis due to the unequal distribution of male and female participants in the sample; its inclusion did not materially alter the estimated direct or indirect effects.ResultsThe desire for being liked was positively associated with smartphone addiction (B = 0.713, p < 0.001), whereas both the desire for being liked (B = −0.137, p = 0.004) and smartphone addiction (B = −0.066, p = 0.006) were negatively associated with psychological resilience. The indirect association between the desire for being liked and psychological resilience through smartphone addiction was statistically significant (indirect effect B = −0.047, 95% bootstrap CI [−0.094, −0.011]). The observed covariance pattern was compatible with the proposed mediation model; however, the final model explained a modest proportion of the variance in psychological resilience (R2 = 0.099).ConclusionThe findings indicate that a stronger tendency to seek social approval was associated with higher levels of smartphone addiction and lower levels of psychological resilience. Smartphone addiction showed a statistically significant indirect association in the relationship between the desire for being liked and psychological resilience. Given the cross-sectional design and the modest explanatory power of the model, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects and may contribute to understanding psychosocial adjustment among university students in sports sciences.

articles.title: Interpersonal communication competence, organizational climate, and academic burnout: examining indirect associations within the job demands–resources framework
articles.author: Batıkan Güngör Çağıran
articles.summary: AimThis study examined associations among organizational climate, interpersonal communication competence, and academic burnout among university faculty within the Job Demands–Resources framework, with particular attention to the indirect association involving communication competence.MethodsCross-sectional survey data were obtained from 406 full-time faculty members in the Gainesville, Florida region of the United States. PLS-SEM analyses were conducted using SmartPLS 4. The model was assessed using a two-stage Mode A PLS-SEM procedure with 5,000 bootstrap resamples and percentile 95% confidence intervals. First-order organizational climate and burnout dimensions were assessed before their scores were used at the higher-order level; interpersonal communication competence was modeled reflectively using 10 items.ResultsOrganizational climate was positively associated with interpersonal communication competence (β = 0.399, p < 0.001). Organizational climate (β = −0.416, p < 0.001) and communication competence (β = −0.327, p < 0.001) were negatively associated with academic burnout. The indirect association was also statistically significant (β = −0.131, 95% CI [−0.175, −0.091]).

articles.title: A study on age group differences in gender awareness among female employees in the hotel industry
articles.author: Hui Wang
articles.summary: IntroductionWomen constitute a growing share of the hospitality workforce. Differences in gender consciousness between younger and older female hotel employees remain under-explored, particularly outside Western contexts, as do the factors that account for them.MethodsThis study examined such differences among 302 female hotel employees in China, drawing on an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design in which a structured survey of two age groups (151 aged 18 to 44 and 151 aged 45 and above) was followed by semi-structured interviews of ten employees (five from each age group). Grounded in social role theory and generational cohort theory, the survey examined two related gender-relevant constructs, feminine communal orientation and gender equality awareness, while interview data were used to explore participants’ interpretations of the observed differences.ResultsYounger employees showed significantly higher feminine communal orientation and more egalitarian gender attitudes than middle-aged and older employees in the primary group comparisons. After adjustment for educational attainment, hotel-industry tenure, and job level, the age-group difference in feminine communal orientation was attenuated and no longer statistically significant, whereas the difference in gender equality awareness remained significant. Interview participants attributed these differences to three factors, namely educational attainment and knowledge structure, exposure to media and information technology, and changes in social environment and family structure.DiscussionCohort membership in this workforce was closely intertwined with tenure, job level, and educational composition. The findings extend gender consciousness research, previously concentrated in media, education, and general labor market settings, into the hospitality workforce, and they suggest that uniform human resource policies may serve this workforce poorly. Practical implications include transparent promotion criteria, gender-neutral job design, and needs-responsive gender-awareness initiatives aimed at supporting female employees across different career circumstances.

articles.title: Confidence–performance relationships in prospective and retrospective metacognition across local and global judgments
articles.author: Yuki Otomo
articles.summary: Metacognition is the ability to take an objective perspective on one’s own task performance, both retrospectively and prospectively. Although retrospective metacognition has been extensively studied, prospective metacognition remains poorly understood. Previous studies report that prospective metacognitive accuracy is typically lower than retrospective metacognitive accuracy. This pattern has sometimes been interpreted to suggest that prospective metacognition is inherently limited. The present study examined prospective and retrospective metacognition under different informational conditions, focusing on local judgments concerning individual trials and global judgments concerning multiple trials. Participants performed a perceptual detection task and provided confidence ratings before or after task performance, either for individual trials (local judgments) or for five-trial segments (global judgments). The relationship between task performance and confidence was analyzed using a generalized linear mixed-effects logistic regression model that separated within-participant and participant-condition mean confidence components. Within-participant confidence was positively associated with task performance in both retrospective conditions, with a stronger association for local than global judgments. In contrast, within-participant associations were not statistically significant in either prospective condition and were significantly weaker than their retrospective counterparts. The within-participant slopes did not significantly differ between local and global prospective judgments. Participant-condition mean confidence was positively associated with performance in all four conditions. These findings highlight the need to distinguish associations between participants’ mean confidence and performance from sensitivity to variations in performance within participants. The limited evidence for within-participant prospective sensitivity is consistent with constraints on information available before stimulus presentation, although the present findings do not establish the source of these limitations.

articles.title: The impact of telework intensity on employee proactive behavior: based on the uncertainty management theory
articles.author: Yixin Zhang
articles.summary: PurposeThis study investigates how telework intensity differentially influences three theoretically differentiated foci of employees’ proactive behavior, drawing on uncertainty management theory and media richness theory. It specifically examines the mediating role of perceived uncertainty and explores how media richness of communication technologies serves as a critical boundary condition in this process.Design/methodology/approachA two-wave, matched leader-employee survey was conducted, collecting data from 212 employees and 81 supervisors across multiple provinces in China. The proposed moderated mediation model was analyzed using SPSS and Mplus.FindingsResults reveal that telework intensity directly increases employees’ perception of uncertainty, which in turn indirectly reduces prosocial and pro-organization foci proactive behaviors, but does not significantly affect pro-self foci proactive behavior. Media richness significantly moderates this effect: higher media richness weakens the positive relationship between telework intensity and the perception of uncertainty.OriginalityThis study shifts the focus in telework research from general outcomes to a nuanced examination of proactive behavior across distinct foci. It introduces and empirically validates media richness as a pivotal technological moderator, clarifying both how telework intensity influences employees and under what technological conditions its effects are attenuated.

articles.title: A multi-study exploratory investigation into choking under pressure frequency, self-compassion, and depressive symptoms in athletes
articles.author: Christopher Mesagno
articles.summary: This exploratory, quantitative multi-study paper aims to determine if self-compassion moderates the relationship between choking under pressure (i.e., choking) frequency and depressive symptoms. In Study 1, 213 athletes who currently competed in, or recently retired from, competitive sport agreed to complete a survey that included demographics information, choking frequency in the last year of sport participation, self-compassion scale, and depressive symptoms scale, questions. Moderation analysis found no significant moderation effects for self-compassion on choking frequency in the last year and depressive symptoms, which was likely the result of confounding variables in the Study 1 design. Thus, using an independent sample of 303 athletes, a follow-up study (i.e., Study 2) was conducted. Methodological changes included controlling for confounding variables present in Study 1, alongside choking frequency measured within the last 3 months and 1 month. Study 2 findings indicated that a positive relationship between choking frequency and depressive symptoms exists. Furthermore, a significant moderation effect occurred for self-compassion on choking frequency within the last 3 months and depressive symptoms in the overall sample. Athletes with low self-compassion showed stronger positive associations between choking frequency within the last 3 months and depressive symptoms, while those with higher self-compassion exhibited resilience to the negative effects of choking. This multi-study paper was the first study, to date, to identify that self-compassion may moderate the association between choking frequency and adverse mental health outcomes, such that lower self-compassion may heighten vulnerability, whereas higher self-compassion may provide a potential protective buffer, to adverse mental health consequences following choking experiences.

articles.title: Beyond social skills: emotion regulation as a potential mechanism linking physical exercise to social anxiety in left-behind adolescents
articles.author: Li Wu
articles.summary: IntroductionThis cross-sectional, exploratory study investigated the association between physical exercise (PE) and social anxiety (SA) among 862 left-behind adolescents in China. It examined emotion regulation abilities (ERA) and peer relationships (PR) as potential mediators and gender as a moderator in this association.MethodsA cross-sectional exploratory design was adopted. Participants were 862 Chinese left-behind adolescents. Path analysis was used to test the hypothesized sequential mediation model and gender moderation effect.ResultsPath analysis revealed that PE was negatively associated with SA. Each separate path of the hypothesized sequential chain (PE → ERA, ERA → PR, PR → SA) was statistically significant, while the overall sequential mediation effect (PE → ERA → PR → SA) was non-significant (95% CI included zero). This indicated that the significant PE–ERA association had a small effect size and could not propagate fully through the chain to SA. The direct path from PE to PR was also non-significant. The data favoured independent mediation pathways rather than a sequential mediation process. Gender moderated the pathway: the positive PE–ERA association was significant for females but non-significant for males.DiscussionThe findings are hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory and require replication via longitudinal research. For vulnerable adolescents, PE may help build emotional competence, which contributes to improved peer bonds. Interventions could integrate emotion-regulation skill training into physical activity programmes, particularly targeting female adolescents. Due to the cross-sectional nature of the study, causal conclusions cannot be drawn.
